hook: Dolgov has been inside Google and Waymo's self-driving effort from its earliest days as a Google X project through its emergence as the first company to operate paid, fully driverless rides at commercial scale, rising from founding engineer to Co-CEO across that entire arc.
name: Dmitri Dolgov

quote.text: Full autonomy is still one of the hardest technology problems of our time.
quote.context: Attributed in Waymo public communications and interviews on the complexity of driverless technology

reading.body:
Dmitri Dolgov is the engineer who built the technical foundation of Waymo from its first year as a Google X project in 2009 and then led it to the first commercial, fully driverless robotaxi service in history, a span of roughly fourteen years from founding engineer to Co-CEO.

The timeline here is notable for its continuity. Dolgov did not arrive after the hard problems were solved. He was present at the origin, held the CTO role through the transition from Google project to independent Alphabet company, and was in technical command when Waymo ran its first no-safety-driver rides in Phoenix in 2020. That unbroken arc from 2009 to the Co-CEO appointment in 2023 is unusual in a field where leadership often turns over before a product reaches the public.

For autonomous vehicles, the relevance to compute and infrastructure is real but indirect in this data. Waymo's progression from test vehicles to commercial service implies sustained scaling of sensing hardware, software, and the compute required to train and validate driving models, but the data here documents Dolgov's role and titles, not the underlying infrastructure. What the data does not cover is fleet size, compute spend, energy footprint, or the operational details of expansion to additional cities. His own framing, that full autonomy remains one of the hardest technology problems of the time, is consistent with a field where the engineering ceiling is still being discovered rather than closed.

quick_facts: Joined Google's self-driving car project in 2009, one of its earliest engineers
Named Waymo's Chief Technology Officer, leading its driving technology
Became Waymo Co-CEO in 2023, alongside Tekedra Mawakana
Holds a PhD in robotics from the University of Michigan

achievements.title: Founding engineer, Google self-driving car project (2009)
achievements.impact: One of the small original team that built the technology underlying Waymo.

achievements.title: Chief Technology Officer, Waymo
achievements.impact: Directed the engineering behind Waymo's driving software and sensor systems as the company scaled from test vehicles to commercial robotaxi service.

achievements.title: Waymo's fully driverless commercial launch (Phoenix, 2020)
achievements.impact: Under his technical leadership, Waymo became the first company to offer rider-only, no-safety-driver rides to the public.

achievements.title: Named Co-CEO of Waymo (2023)
achievements.impact: Elevated to joint chief executive as Waymo expanded driverless service to additional U.S. cities.
